answer.evidence: The formula is in radon/metrics.py:98-117 (mi_compute). It computes 171 - 5.2*ln(V) - 0.23*G - 16.2*ln(SLOC) + 50*sin(sqrt(2.46*radians(comments))), then scales by 100/171 and clamps to [0, 100]. Review points: (1) the early return of 100.0 when volume or sloc is <= 0 hides empty or degenerate input. (2) Comment percentage is passed through math.radians. That is a deliberate trick to reproduce the original 2.46*sqrt(perCM) term, but it should be checked against the reference formula. (3) The clamp should be tested at both ends. Complexity is the branch score G, and it feeds the formula as a plain additive term. Its upstream computation in radon/complexity.py (the block and function cyclomatic-complexity aggregation) and the Halstead/visit logic in radon/visitors.py (operator and operand counting, which determines volume) set the inputs, so I would spend equal time checking that those values are correct and consistently typed before they reach mi_compute. radon/raw.py only supplies line counts, so it needs no separate pass beyond confirming how sloc and comment counts are passed in by mi_parameters.
